blocks.orig: Nairobi is the capital and the largest city of Kenya. The name comes from the Maasai phrase Enkare Nairobi. This means “cool water“, a reference to the Nairobi River which flows through the city. The city has the nickname Green City in the Sun.
blocks.html: Kenya's capital and biggest city is Nairobi. Its name derives from the Maasai words Enkare Nairobi, meaning “cool water“, which refers to the Nairobi River running through the city. Nairobi also goes by the nickname Green City in the Sun.

blocks.orig: Nairobi was founded in 1899 by British East Africa, as a rail depot on the Uganda Railway. After that, the town quickly grew to replace Mombasa as the capital of Kenya in 1907. As a result, it became the capital of the Republic of Kenya after independence in 1963. Until today it is the centre for the colony’s coffee, tea and sisal industry.
blocks.html: British East Africa established Nairobi in 1899 as a rail depot on the Uganda Railway. The town expanded so fast that by 1907 it had taken over from Mombasa as Kenya's capital, and when the country gained independence in 1963 it became the capital of the Republic of Kenya. To this day it remains the heart of the coffee, tea and sisal industries that date back to colonial times.

blocks.orig: The modern world has quickly caught up with the city. A frontier town no more, Nairobi is one of Africa’s largest, and most interesting cities today. Nairobi is a city that never seems to sleep. The entire town has a boundless energy, and is thriving place where all of human life can be found. This is a place of great contrasts where race, tribe and origin all become facets of its unique character. The city has not lost its sense of the past. With an excellent museum and the historical home of Karen Blixen, author of Out of Africa open to visitors. Home to thousands of businesses, international companies and organizations, Nairobi is an established hub for business and culture.
blocks.html: Modern life has swiftly overtaken the city. No longer a frontier town, Nairobi now ranks among Africa's biggest and most fascinating cities, and it is a place that never really seems to sleep. Boundless energy runs through the whole town, a thriving place where every side of human life is on show. It is a city of sharp contrasts, in which race, tribe and origin all form part of its singular character. At the same time, Nairobi has kept hold of its past: there is an excellent museum, and the historic home of Karen Blixen, who wrote Out of Africa, is open to visitors. With thousands of businesses, international companies and organisations based here, Nairobi is a well-established centre of business and culture.

blocks.orig: A short drive from downtown Nairobi is the Nairobi National Park. The wide, open grass plain begins right on the city limits and is home to a variety of wildlife, including lions, leopards, cheetahs, hyenas, buffalo, giraffes and a diverse bird life with over 400 species.  And it is also the most popular place to see the endangered black rhinos and they owe the park its nickname “Kifaru” (rhinoceros), of which there are still more than 50 here.
blocks.html: Nairobi National Park lies only a short drive from the city centre. Its wide, open grassland starts right at the city boundary and shelters a range of wildlife: lions, leopards, cheetahs, hyenas, buffalo, giraffes and a rich birdlife of more than 400 species.  It is also the best-known place to see the endangered black rhino, of which more than 50 still live here, and it is to them that the park owes its nickname “Kifaru” (rhinoceros).

blocks.orig: Next to it you will find the well-regarded elephant orphanage operated by the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust. It works to protect elephants, rhinos and giraffes and runs the world’s most successful rescue and rehabilitation program for orphaned animals.
blocks.html: Right beside the park sits the highly regarded elephant orphanage of the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, which protects elephants, rhinos and giraffes and operates the most successful rescue and rehabilitation programme for orphaned animals anywhere in the world.

blocks.orig: Nairobi is also used as a jumping-off point for safari trips to the Masai Mara Natural Reserve.
blocks.html: Nairobi also serves as a starting point for safaris to the Masai Mara Natural Reserve.

blocks.orig: The Masai Mara Natural Reserve  is one of the largest game reserves in Africa and is around 270 km from the capital Nairobi – only around 45 minutes’ flight time. It is home to over 95 species of mammals and over 400 species of birds and is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Kenya.
blocks.html: Among Africa's largest game reserves, the Masai Mara Natural Reserve lies roughly 270 km from the capital Nairobi, a flight of only about 45 minutes. With more than 95 mammal species and over 400 bird species, it ranks among Kenya's most visited tourist destinations.

blocks.orig: Another attraction is the Solio Ranch, a fenced, privately owned sanctuary dedicated to the protection of rhinos.  The ranch is located in the valley between the high slopes of Mount Kenya and the peaks of the Aberdare Mountains just north of Nairobi. Up to 40 Rhinos live here in harmony with other wildlife, including buffalo, zebra, giraffe and flat game such as eland, oryx, impala, waterbuck, Thompson’s gazelle and warthog.
blocks.html: Solio Ranch is another draw: a fenced sanctuary in private hands, devoted entirely to rhino conservation.  You'll find it in the valley between the high slopes of Mount Kenya and the Aberdare peaks, just north of Nairobi. As many as 40 rhinos share the ranch peacefully with other animals, among them buffalo, zebra, giraffe and plains game such as eland, oryx, impala, waterbuck, Thompson's gazelle and warthog.

blocks.orig: It takes about an hour flight time to reach Nairobi from Kilimanjaro international airport in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Flying in from Kilimanjaro international airport in Tanzania, you reach Nairobi in about an hour.

blocks.orig: Travel Tips from our experts about Nairobi

My name is Harrison and I am a guide in Nairobi for 22 years. Most of our guests are impressed how busy and vibrant Nairobi is. It offers so much! You can be in a huge shopping mall in the morning and bottle feeding a baby rhino in the afternoon.
blocks.html: I'm Harrison, and I have worked as a guide in Nairobi for 22 years. What strikes most of our guests is how busy and lively Nairobi is. There is so much on offer: spend the morning in an enormous shopping mall and the afternoon bottle-feeding a baby rhino.

blocks.orig: How long to stay? At least 1-2 days, depending on what you are planning to do
blocks.html: How long should you stay? A minimum of 1-2 days, depending on your plans

blocks.orig: Giraffe Manor is an exklusive Boutique-Hotel and one of the most famous ones in the world! One of the most fascinating things about Giraffe Manor is the resident herd of Rothschild’s giraffes, who stick their long necks through the windows in the morning and in the evening in the hope of a reward before retreating to their forest reserve.
blocks.html: Giraffe Manor is an exclusive boutique hotel, and one of the best known anywhere in the world! Its most captivating feature is the resident herd of Rothschild's giraffes, which poke their long necks through the windows each morning and evening hoping for a treat, before heading back to their forest reserve.

blocks.orig: Nairobi is a modern city. It is one of Africa’s largest, and most interesting cities and never seems to sleep. The entire town has a boundless energy, and is thriving place. Nairobi and its surrounding area offers many attractions and is also used as a jumping-off point for safari trips to the Masai Mara Natural Reserve.
blocks.html: Nairobi is a modern city, among the largest and most fascinating in Africa, and it never seems to sleep. Boundless energy runs through the whole town, a thriving place indeed. Nairobi and the area around it offer plenty of attractions, and the city also acts as a starting point for safaris to the Masai Mara Natural Reserve.
